label: Intercompany governance
query: How should intercompany lending be governed so Lakeshore avoids sloppy AFR and true-up failures?
answer:
My read: For Lakeshore Holdings, intercompany lending governance has to sit on top of your existing SAP S/4HANA / NetSuite intercompany footprint and be run like a mini capital-markets function — with a single holdco rulebook, formal ownership at each opco, and automated AFR / true‑up controls baked into the ERP, not spreadsheets. Why (specific to Lakeshore): You already have separate intercompany processes in at least five ERPs (Holdco and Northline on SAP S/4HANA; Brightmark on SAP ECC/Coupa; Forge & Field and Great Lakes Pantry on NetSuite). That fragmentation is exactly how AFR mismatches and missed true‑ups show up at quarter close. Board reporting is already flagging “systems fragmentation and renewal concentration” as a risk, while guidance emphasizes treasury visibility and data platform modernization. Intercompany lending that isn’t tightly governed will directly undercut those board priorities.

Decision fork: If the priority is audit/AFR assurance: centralize policy and approvals at Holdco and enforce strict, low‑flex templates across all opcos, even if it slows some local optimization. If the priority is capital agility: allow more local structuring, but require stronger automated reconciliations, daily position reporting, and tighter materiality thresholds for manual overrides. What I would do next:

1) Establish a Holdco Intercompany Lending Policy approved by CFO / Group Treasurer that locks down: pricing bands, FX rules, documentation standards, cut‑off times, and true‑up cadence.
